newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up sharply on firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up sharply on firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended up sharply Tuesday in an active session, with more fund buying and firmer physical prices rallying the complex, particularly front months, market sources said.
September rallied 10.2 cents to close at $2.528 per million British thermal units. October settled 8.7 cents higher at $2.532. Most others ended steady to up 8.7 cents.

"It's a classic squeeze. Cash continues to move up despite the (mild) weather because people are short the physical. I don't see it letting up yet," said one Midwest trader, noting funds were reported to be buying front months again today.

With cash a dime over the screen and concerns lingering about inventory levels, traders saw few reasons for prices to retreat much anytime soon despite mostly mild U.S. weather this week and forecasts for more of the same during bidweek next week.

Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 62 bcf to 90 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 93 bcf. Stocks are almost 10 percent below the three year average.

Technical traders noted September on ACCESS broke the $2.55 resistance point. They pegged next resistance at the contract high and double top of $2.605. Further selling was likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was still seen at Friday's low of $2.395 and then at $2.34 and $2.30. Better buying was expected in the $2.25-2.27 area.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed about a nickel to the high-$2.50s. Midcon pipes were up a couple of cents to mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas also firmed a few cents to about the $2.80 level.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip jumped five cents to $2.403. NYMEX said 68,384 contracts traded, up sharply from Monday's revised tally of 35,245.
On the KCBT, September finished 11 cents higher at $2.465, while deferreds ended up by three to 9.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 6.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
